figures.title: Chapter map: 12 parts, one sign convention
figures.why: the subject is a chain — each part's formula is the last one with one index flipped; the map shows the reading spine and where the playbook sits
figures.data: parts 1–2 rays & mirrors; 3–4 refraction & TIR; 5 prisms & dispersion; 6 lenses & systems; 7 eye & instruments; 8 Olympiad machinery; 9 playbook; 10–11 paper; 12 formula sheet
figures.read: an image chain is just one arrow per element — read parts 1–8 in order, then revise from part 9
figures.source: course overview (How these notes are organised)

figures.title: Mirror: one formula, sign before algebra
figures.why: the mirror has exactly one formula, and the signs are the whole method; filling them in before solving turns every curved-mirror question into a substitution
figures.data: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f = 2/R, m = −v/u; concave f < 0, convex f > 0; real object u < 0; v > 0 → same side (real), m < 0 → inverted
figures.read: do not 'fix' signs afterwards — a negative v for a concave mirror is the answer, and it means a real image in front

figures.title: Snell's law: μ₁ sin i = μ₂ sin r
figures.why: refraction is one equation plus one rule — which way it bends, and how the deviation splits; the flow pins both to the index ratio
figures.data: μ₁ sin i = μ₂ sin r, μ = c/v, μ₂₁ = μ₂/μ₁ = v₁/v₂ = λ₁/λ₂; into denser bends toward the normal, δ = i − r; frequency unchanged, wavelength falls to λ/μ
figures.read: 'optically denser' means higher index, full stop — turpentine floats on water yet is optically denser than it

figures.title: Total internal reflection: beyond sin C
figures.why: TIR is Snell's law running out of solutions — nothing new, just the boundary case; the flow states when a ray stops crossing and starts reflecting
figures.data: sin C = μ₂/μ₁ (lower over higher) for μ₁ > μ₂; sin C = 1/μ in air; beyond C no refracted ray exists; conditions: denser → rarer and i ≥ C
figures.read: the incident medium's index sits under the other one — take the sine of the lower over the higher

figures.title: Lens and mirror: the same formula, one index flipped
figures.why: a mirror is a lens with μ₂ = −μ₁, so one sign machine covers both — memorise the surface formula and you never relearn ray optics
figures.data: lens 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, m = v/u, lensmaker 1/f = (μ−1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂), P = 1/f; single surface μ₂/v − μ₁/u = (μ₂−μ₁)/R; mirror is n₂ = −n₁
figures.read: a lens is two surfaces whose intermediate image cancels — turn it around and f is unchanged

figures.title: Triage: six branches, one chain
figures.why: fifteen seconds picking the branch decides which two formulas apply; the hardest step is naming the object for the next element
figures.data: which element → which image is the next object (O → I₁ → I₂, one formula per arrow) → sign every distance → what is actually asked (position, nature, magnification, angle)
figures.read: the second box — real or virtual object for the next element — is where most marks are lost
